metadata.title: GAPMA: Graph-Attention Cell Usage Prediction with Polarity-Minimized NPN Aggregation for Design-Specific Cell Composition (MLCAD 2026 Artifact)
metadata.description:
Artifact for MLCAD 2026 paper 179, GAPMA: Graph-Attention Cell Usage Prediction with Polarity-Minimized NPN Aggregation for Design-Specific Cell Composition.

The archive is the training-data-generation, GATv2-training, and iterative candidate-cell-selection pipeline described in the paper. It selects a small set of custom standard cells to add to a minimal baseline library for a given RTL design, before any cell layout exists, and measures the resulting post-route cell-area reduction.

Contents. Ten Verilog RTL benchmarks (five training, five evaluation), a curated 41 MB subset of the SO3 academic 3 nm PDK, the mining and feature-extraction and GATv2 demand-prediction code with a pretrained checkpoint, and three top-level entry points: flow/datagen.sh (training-data generation), flow/train_gat.sh (GATv2 training), and flow/autorun.sh (the D0 baseline through D3 iterative candidate-cell-selection loop).

Dependencies. The full pipeline invokes Synopsys Fusion Compiler for synthesis and place-and-route, and Cadence Pegasus, Quantus, and Liberate for the characterization and extraction steps. These are commercial, license-gated EDA tools not included here. The ILP-based cell-layout-generation step needs a Gurobi license, for which academic users can use the free academic tier. Reviewers without EDA-tool access can still inspect the full source, the curated PDK, and the pretrained model, and can run the Python-only mining and GATv2 inference code.

Submodules. The three public submodules (Yosys, OpenDB, SO3-Cell) are present as empty directories. Their upstream URLs are in .gitmodules.

No confidential credentials, license files, or full commercial PDK contents are included. Corresponds to GAPMA repository commit f5615008652163648ae1c24c8df2d012e851bce5.

metadata.title: RF-LEGO: Artifact Evaluation Package (MobiCom '26)
metadata.description:
Artifact-evaluation package for RF-LEGO, a modular RF sensing framework combining signal-processing structure with trainable deep-unrolled modules. Contains the rflego implementation, three pretrained module weights, six prepared real-world held-out benchmarks, a one-click Colab notebook, and evaluation, plotting, and cascadability scripts. The workflow runs on a plain CPU with the shipped weights, is deterministic under seed 42, and completes in 2-3 minutes.

Licensing: the source code and the pretrained weights are released under the MIT license; the prepared benchmark files under ae_data/ are released under CC BY 4.0.

metadata.title: Artifact of "Automatically Generating ML Compiler Backends from Tensor Accelerator ISA Descriptions"
metadata.description:
This is the artifact for our paper on automatically generating sound and complete compiler backends for tensor accelerators from their ISA descriptions written in TAIDL.

This artifact consists of ACT source code, TAIDL ISA definitions, input kernel benchmarks, and the necessary scripts to reproduce the evaluation results. To facilitate artifact evaluation, we have automated the entire environment setup and experimental processes as part of Docker images.

The artifact can be downloaded by clicking "Download all" below or by clicking here.
Then, unzip the downloaded artifact (named "21926083.zip") twice as follows:
unzip 21926083.zip
unzip act-artifact-oopsla26.zip
cd act-artifact-oopsla26-master

GitHub repo of the artifact: https://github.com/act-compiler/act-artifact-oopsla26. Note that this repository is now archived (read-only).
For more recent releases, refer to https://github.com/act-compiler/act

metadata.title: Artifact for "Ariadne: An Efficient Deadlock-Free Temporal RDA with Local Tags and Interleaved Switching"
metadata.description:
This artifact accompanies the MICRO 2026 paper “Ariadne: An Efficient
Deadlock-Free Temporal RDA with Local Tags and Interleaved Switching.”

It contains two components:

  1. A Scala-based configuration generator and cycle-level temporal simulator.

  2. Vivado and Vitis 2021.1 projects for FPGA behavioral simulation on an
    AMD/Xilinx VCU128 platform with a MicroBlaze processor. The FPGA package is

    evaluation.

The simulator package includes the Scala source code, benchmark configurations,
SBT build files, Windows workflow scripts, and log-parsing utilities required
to run and validate nine temporal CGRA workloads. The supplementary FPGA
package includes Vivado reconstruction scripts, prebuilt hardware and software
files, implementation reports, and a reference ATAX behavioral-simulation
waveform.

metadata.title: VolTRE: Uniform Sampling for Timed Regular Expressions (EMSOFT 2026 artifact)
metadata.description:
This is the artifact accompanying the paper "Uniform Sampling for Timed Regular
Expressions", submitted for artifact evaluation at EMSOFT 2026.

The paper introduces the first method to uniformly sample timed words directly
from timed regular expressions (TREs). Given a desired length and duration as
input, the method guarantees that all words of that length and duration in the
language have the same chance of being drawn. It also introduces the first
technique for treating the full class of timed regular languages recognized by
non-deterministic timed automata (excluding those that require silent
transitions), whereas previous work handled only deterministic timed automata.
The approach is implemented in VolTRE, an open-source prototype tool.

This archive packages VolTRE together with the experiment scripts, data, and a
Docker environment needed to reproduce the paper's figures. The bundled wordgen
tool (GPLv3, see NOTICE) is included only as a comparison baseline.

metadata.title: Artifact for "AMG: AMX–GPU Cooperative Acceleration of Billion-Scale ANNS via GEMM Reformulation" (MICRO 2026)
metadata.description:
Artifact for "AMG: AMX–GPU Cooperative Acceleration of Billion-Scale ANNS via GEMM Reformulation" (MICRO 2026)

This artifact contains the source code, build scripts, run scripts, and plotting scripts for AMG, a billion-scale approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) system that cooperatively accelerates IVF search across an AMX-capable Intel Xeon CPU and an NVIDIA GPU via GEMM reformulation.

The artifact reproduces the three key experimental results of the paper: (1) end-to-end performance (QPS) of IVF-CPU, IVF-UVM, IVF-UVM+QG, RUMMY, RUMMY+QG, and AMG on DEEP1B, SIFT1B, and TEXT1B (Fig. 11); (2) an ablation study of AMG on SIFT1B, normalized to IVF-CPU (Fig. 12); and (3) a throughput comparison between RUMMY and AMG under emulated PCIe 6.0, PCIe 7.0, and NVLink 5.0 interconnects (Fig. 19).

Experiments require a server with an AVX-512/AMX-capable Intel Xeon (Granite Rapids) CPU and an NVIDIA H100 GPU, together with the DEEP1B, SIFT1B, and TEXT1B datasets and prebuilt billion-scale IVF indexes. Each of the three experiments resides in its own directory (end_to_end/, ablation_study/, and throughput_comparison/) and is driven by its own resumable run_all.sh script, which executes all runs and regenerates the corresponding figure in PDF/PNG format. Note that the end_to_end experiment must be run before throughput_comparison, as the latter reuses its RUMMY results. See README.md for build instructions and detailed usage.

metadata.title: Trace2Skill: Verifier-Guided Skill Evolution for Long-Context EDA Agents (MLCAD 2026 Artifact)
metadata.description:
Artifact for the MLCAD 2026 paper Trace2Skill: Verifier-Guided Skill Evolution for Long-Context EDA Agents. This snapshot contains the Trace2Skill optimizer, recovered NeMo Gym CVDP runtime, portable C3/C4 configurations, a revision-pinned CVDP subset downloader, cached evidence that deterministically recomputes the reported results, and two representative action traces.

The offline validator reports C3 as 173/640 passing optimization rollouts (27.03125%, with a pass on 3/8 tasks) and C4 as 215/640 (33.59375%, with a pass on 6/8 tasks). Live hosted-model reruns are optional and stochastic because immutable historical provider revisions and sampling seeds were not retained. Release tag v1.0.0 corresponds to Git commit 5702b3fe739ce33013296759162ad771ee11bd36.

metadata.title: ScopeInsert: A Sanitized Reproducibility Artifact for Scope-Aware C++ Insertion Testing
metadata.description:
ScoWe is a reviewer-facing runnable artifact for our scope-aware C++ insertion-testing workflow. This release is intentionally sanitized and packaged as a binary reproduction bundle: it includes the runnable jar, replay scripts, grammar resources, and public issue seeds required to reproduce the main workflow described in the paper, while omitting the Java source tree.

Included in this artifact:
- the runnable 2.0.jar binary;
- BraceMatcher-based slicing support via the packaged replay scripts;
- grammar/cpp and PowerShell scripts for issue-seed preparation, slicing, generation, and local checking;
- the public reviewer seed corpus under artifact-data/scowe/issue-reproducers.

Intentionally excluded:
- the Java source tree and repository-wide development files;
- unrelated or unpublished generators and experiments for other languages and pipelines;
- repository-wide outputs and paper-authoring materials.

Quick reproduction: prepare issue seeds, slice them, and run the bundled ScoWe jar on the sliced corpus. The packaged README describes the exact commands and expected output directories.

hits.title: ScopeInsert: A Sanitized Reproducibility Artifact for Scope-Aware C++ Insertion Testing

metadata.title: Approximate FrodoKEM-640 Artifact for "Replacing Explicit Error Generation With Approximate Computing in LWE-Based Schemes" - CASES2026
metadata.description:
This artifact provides the AxFrodoKEM software implementation, developed by CEA LIST. It is derived from a modified version of the original FrodoKEM implementation to allow the use of approximate operators, reduce data structures, and minimize the pseudo-random bits generated with SHAKE.

It accompanies the paper "Replacing Explicit Error Generation With Approximate Computing in LWE-Based Schemes" submitted to CASES 2026. The repository provides the necessary C-models and execution workflows (using NIST Known Answer Test vectors) to independently verify the Decryption Failure Rate (DFR) and structural claims discussed in the paper.

metadata.title: PNMAX: Mapping-Architecture Co-Exploration Framework for Processing Near Memory (MICRO 2026 Artifact)
metadata.description: Artifact for the MICRO 2026 paper "PNMAX: Mapping-Architecture Co-Exploration Framework for Processing Near Memory." PNMAX is a design-space-exploration framework for processing near memory (PNM) systems that co-explores workload mappings and architecture configurations, combining a graph-based parameterized architecture model (GPAM), a per-component PPA characterization database, and an analytical cost model validated against the UniNDP and AttAcc simulators. This archive contains the source code of the framework, the baseline simulators, and a top-level makefile that reproduce every figure and table in the paper. See README.md for setup and reproduction.
